goalbuddy_receipt_v1.summary: User-facing claim: Phase 4 Slice 2 now provides durable, canvas-first Type, Select, Drag, and multi-target Hold authoring through the same typed service operations used by the CLI, with deterministic browser-native HTML/CSS output, native-animation scrubbing, exact history, responsive/keyboard access, reduced-motion behavior, and discrete-boundary visual proof. Fresh installed-Chrome QA found and test-first fixed one transient zero-width resize error. Slice 3, Phase 5, publication, push, pull request, and merge work were not started.

evidence: Complete workflow inventory: installed Chrome created Hold, Type, Select, and Drag in order; Hold retained two animated targets, Type used stepped text reveal, Select used real keyboard plus canvas targeting, and Drag exposed three waypoint handles including an intermediate 400 ms point.

Durability and fail-closed behavior: the dragged intermediate waypoint committed at revision 5 and survived reload; an invalid Hold update reported that revision 5 was unchanged, then a valid boundary update retained both targets and committed revision 6.

Playback and layout: Play advanced the native preview from 401 ms to 500 ms before Pause; Chrome containment measured 18..742 within a 760 px viewport and 24..1256 within a 1280 px viewport with no workspace overflow.

Chrome diagnostics after the regression fix: full-page capture produced zero editor-origin errors. The aggregate browser receipt reports runtimeErrorCount=0, failedRequestCount=0, httpErrorCount=0, and unexpectedNetworkCount=0.

Deterministic repeated export: two complete installed-Chrome runs produced the same receipt digest dc4ef6e8a990f1fa40913d1c4d4ee4b2d2bf3fbf8ab18d127337c8649738d14f, browser proof digest ae488c8cf7d681714d462794161ace560b05ac5370cc1a541670bcd7b04392d8, and visual proof digest d8e725dac2ab22c414c323c3bd381436630d585d2dbf3d91a2a082fceb4e9d2b.

Visual equivalence around discrete boundaries: 29 sampled frames, 30 expected boundary assertions, two raster runs, 19 distinct rasters, maximum repeated pixel difference 0, and zero unexpected requests. Samples cover every Type step and Select, Drag, and Hold boundaries on both sides.

Reduced motion and native output: browser proof reports four cues at revision 35 and reducedAnimationCount=0; the browser suite positively asserts compiler-exact iframe HTML and CSSAnimation objects rather than a JavaScript interpolator.

Sensitive-content exclusion: the repository scan covered tracked inventory, branch diff, index, worktree, and untracked files with findingCount=0 and privateNeedleCount=0. The private-ignore receipt reports targetCount=3, ignoredCount=3, trackedPrivateCount=0. Package lock and both privacy checker files are unchanged.

Private-only exclusion: the legacy cursor-click-reveal browser spec still requires its intentionally absent ignored private canonical input. The complete public suite excludes only that intrinsic-private spec and passes 35/35; no private input was fabricated or copied.

Scope inspection: changed production surfaces are limited to the approved domain, protocol, service seed, CLI, editor, public synthetic fixture, visual proof, package script, and goal-control files. No Slice 3, Phase 5, database artifact, screenshot, private fixture, branding, publication, or integration work is present.
